title: Guanylate Kinase 1 Deficiency: A Novel and Potentially Treatable Mitochondrial DNA Depletion/Deletions Disease.

reviewer.method: Personally read all375 lines of held PMC manuscript including50 references and all legends; reviewed graphical abstract, all six main figures and all cells of the original clinical Table1 (with a rotated derivative for labels). Manually transcribed table after reading; no automated-read claim. Individually compared both assigned packets,71 phenotypes and three alleles. Supplement unavailable and earns no read credit.

audit.exposure_note: Required HANDOFF reading exposed aggregate history and a historical public-control HG002/FGFR2 case-specific rank. No target-case inference ranks, inference-output files or benchmark outcome summaries consulted. This review is not blinded.

patient_identity.statement: Proband4 is female, current age34, with initial ptosis at16years, matching the packet and clinical Table1. Figure2E anomalously uses a square for the affected proband; narrative and table explicitly female.
limitations: Figure2E conflicts with narrative/table sex; do not silently substitute male.

genotype.statement: Proband4 has heterozygous maternal start-codon c.2T>G and paternal c.139C>T/p.Gln47Ter in long transcript NM_001159390; source predicts p.Leu2_Met22del for the start change whereas packet conservatively uses p.Met1?.
limitations: Transcript/protein accession versions and hg38 genomic conversions are not independently remapped in this source review. Protein uncertainty notation is less specific, not a different DNA variant.

segregation.statement: Sanger testing identifies maternal c.2T>G and paternal c.139C>T in unaffected heterozygous parents.

phase.statement: Parental origins establish the two heterozygous variants in trans.

causal_confidence.statement: The paper attributes mitochondrial DNA maintenance disease to biallelic GUK1 deficiency, supported by muscle mtDNA/respiratory-chain abnormalities, segregation, and functional isoform/cell findings. Probands1–3 supplied fibroblasts; Proband4 did not. This supports source causal attribution, without independently certifying the packet ACMG PATHOGENIC or clinical SOLVED classification.
limitations: No independent clinical validation; treatment observations are in vitro and are not clinical efficacy or prescribing evidence.

phenotype_completeness.statement: Proband4 packet immunodeficiency is contradicted by explicitly normal immunological screening, with no lowCD4 count. Onset16/last34 and major myopathy/ocular findings match; main records lower-limb areflexia. Several broad negative HPO encodings exceed narrower table labels.
limitations: SupplementaryrespiratorychainTable1 unavailable; no numerical supplementary results claimed.
